# When Vem reads from the service

Reuse known information and acquire only what a view still needs.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/data/understand/acquisition


Once a task list has loaded, filtering it should feel instant. Opening another view should reuse the same information. Try both in the app below.

### Experiment: Filter without fetching

Choose To do, open the overview, then open the walk’s notes.

Filtering and the overview reuse the task list. Opening notes asks for a missing field, so it reads once more. Returning to that detail reuses the new information.

Runs a deterministic simulated source with the real Vem runtime. Interactive controls are available in the HTML page; no JavaScript is needed to read this explanation.

## A query describes a need

Vem first projects information it already knows and is allowed to show. Vem combines missing requirements across active consumers, including other tabs, and chooses among the backend capabilities declared by the integration. One response may satisfy several views; existing or in-flight information changes what is worth reading.

### From need to knowledge

1. Collect what active consumers across tabs still need.
2. Subtract known facts and account for work already in flight.
3. Choose compatible reads using coverage, permissions, and cost.
4. Publish actual evidence, then plan for any remaining gaps.

The shared owner combines demand from tabs and imperative readers, subtracts known information, and reuses in-flight work. It compares declared backend capabilities and costs. Responses establish facts; missing information may require another source.

A consumer can also follow existing knowledge with `acquire: false`, or observe work with `useReadStatus`. Neither adds missing-information requirements. These options control whether a consumer asks for data, not how the planner chooses sources. [The display guide](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/build/display#show-known-data-without-requesting-it) shows both.

## What is actually missing?

| The view needs… | What Vem must know |
| --- | --- |
| A list of tasks | Which tasks belong to the collection |
| Task titles | The selected field on each known task |
| Only unfinished tasks | Each candidate's status, even if status is not displayed |
| A definite empty state | Complete membership and enough information to evaluate the filter |

A missing title leaves a known task visible as an incomplete row. A missing status cannot establish whether a task matches the unfinished filter. [Partial results](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/build/partial-results) shows how to render both.

## A query is not a request cache key

Different queries can reuse the same facts. A list response that includes notes can satisfy a later notes view. If a detail response contains only one task's notes, opening a different task needs another read. The response's actual contents determine what becomes known.

To see Vem choose between competing reads across several views, try [the automatic planning example](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/planning#plan-for-the-whole-application).

The definition declares `sources`: available representations, fields, membership, supported filters, and access. Vem plans automatically across the combined demand. [Connect a resource](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/resources) shows the declarations; [how Vem chooses reads](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/planning) explains the selection and its bounds. Feature components only describe information.

## Is this field kept current?

Three questions stay separate: **may I see it**, **what was observed**, and **what keeps that observation current**. Permission answers the first; source responses answer the second; declared event continuity answers the third.

A task's status can be `live` while its notes are a `snapshot` from the last read. An `immutable` field needs no change monitoring because it cannot change for that identity. Vem reports these states per field; an open socket alone does not establish any of them.

Snapshots remain useful without automatic time-based verification. A known gap in the field's declared change coverage makes it stale and can require acquisition. A gap in another field's or project's channel does not. Domain authors [declare that coverage explicitly](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/events#declare-which-fields-the-events-keep-current).

## What makes Vem acquire again?

A new unsatisfied view, retrying unsuccessful acquisition, or a reported event-coverage gap can require new evidence. Mounting, focusing, or waiting a fixed time does not by itself make ordinary data expire.

Events can provide the missing values directly. When an older request finally returns, it cannot overwrite newer established observations or revive values under retired permissions.

<details>
<summary>Measurements that intentionally repeat</summary>

Measurements such as CPU usage are different from ordinary task data. A query can explicitly request a sample interval:


```ts
import { defineResource } from "@hyecompany/vem-data";

export const machines = defineResource<{ usage: number }, { id: string }>()({
	name: "machines",
	fields: ["usage"],
});
export const measuredUsage = machines.get(
	{ id: "web" },
	{
		select: ["usage"],
		sample: { fields: ["usage"], intervalMs: 1000 },
	},
);
```


Import `defineResource` from `@hyecompany/vem-data`. Subscribe with `useQuery(measuredUsage)`. The host also needs a `machines` definition that acquires usage. Sampled fields must be selected; intervals must be finite and at least 100 ms. Sampling ends when consumer demand ends, and does not make unrelated data expire.

</details>

## Why reload might make no request

A reloaded tab can rejoin an owner that still has the needed information. If the owner stopped, a new one can restore eligible data. Permitted values remain displayable, but non-immutable evidence—including plain snapshots—restores stale and the first active need reacquires it. Genuine immutable evidence can survive without another read. This re-establishes evidence after owner loss; it is not a mount, focus, or time-based policy. The integration also establishes the new owner's event continuity. Look at the owner's connection and coverage, not only the page reload, when diagnosing a missing request.


---

# Why information disappears after an access change

Keep readable information and forget only what lost its permission.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/data/understand/access


A task's title can be public while its notes are private. You might be able to read those notes because you belong to a team, because you were invited directly, or both. Try removing each permission.

### Experiment: Who can still read the notes?

Turn off Team access, then the direct invitation.

Either permission can disclose the same private note. Losing both removes the note while the public task survives. A reply captured before withdrawal cannot restore that note after regrant; a new authorized update can.

Runs a deterministic simulated source with the real Vem runtime. Interactive controls are available in the HTML page; no JavaScript is needed to read this explanation.

## A value can have more than one permission

Vem keeps the reasons a value may be shown alongside the value. The domain calls these its **disclosure bases**. If either team access or a direct invitation permits the notes, losing just one should not remove them.

| Change | Visible result |
| --- | --- |
| Team access ends; the invitation remains | Notes remain readable |
| The last permission ends | Notes disappear, including from managed edit drafts |
| Write permission ends, but read access remains | The draft stays; saving is disabled |
| Access is granted again | New authorized evidence can restore the notes |

Derived values and relationships also depend on the information and permissions supporting them. A total computed from unreadable records must not remain visible merely because the total was computed earlier.

## Unknown is different from denied

A fresh owner may not yet know who the caller is. Protected restored data stays hidden until the host identifies the caller. Once the same caller is established, Vem resumes saved permission decisions and makes the supported stale data available immediately. Restarting the browser does not expire those permissions or require a separate permission request for each resource. New decisions and known revocations take precedence.

Quarantine controls what Vem publishes to consumers; it does not encrypt browser storage.

Likewise, a network error during an established session is not a logout. Only an actual access decision or authority retirement withdraws the old permission. A logout can retire private access while leaving public data and the runtime alive.

## An old reply cannot undo withdrawal

A pending read carries the permission generation under which it started. If that permission is retired, the late response cannot repopulate protected data—even if access was granted again in the meantime. Regrant permits new evidence, not reuse of the retired response.

With persistence, Vem records revocation before deleting saved payloads. Live values disappear immediately even if storage fails; the failure must still be reported because durable cleanup was not established.

To implement these rules, follow [access controls step by step](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/access). Components should render managed query and edit values directly: independent copies in React state or a form library need their own withdrawal integration.


---

# What happens when the app closes mid-operation

Keep accepted work separate from what the UI knows about it.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/data/understand/recovery


An app can close after sending a command but before learning what happened. Sending it again could repeat work. Try returning to an unfinished task below.

### Experiment: Return to an unfinished action

Complete the walk, then close and reopen the example.

The first owner records possible submission and sends once. A replacement owner restores its journal and investigates. Missing confirmation leaves the result unknown; recovery never resubmits the command.

Runs a deterministic simulated source with the real Vem runtime. Interactive controls are available in the HTML page; no JavaScript is needed to read this explanation.

## Sending, watching, and showing are separate

| What happened | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| You navigate away | The shared owner can continue observing the action |
| You dismiss its notice | Feedback is acknowledged; server work is unchanged |
| You lose permission to see it | Protected details disappear; accepted work may continue |
| The owner stops before receiving a result | The next owner needs evidence before deciding what happened |

## Recovery investigates

When storage works, Vem records that submission may occur **before** dispatch. An operation ID returned by the backend can then be saved as recovery metadata. After interruption, the domain's `recover` function uses that metadata to check the backend's operation record.

### Recovery investigates what happened

1. Record possible submission before sending, when storage works.
2. A lost response does not tell us whether the work happened.
3. Restore the action record after access is established.
4. Check what happened. Do not send the command again.

A missing response, missing journal, or missing operation history does not prove that the operation never happened. Recovery is not an instruction to submit again. A lock protects owner exclusivity; a heartbeat timeout cannot transfer ownership.

If the operation record proves success, recovery may report success. If the record is absent or no useful metadata survived, the truthful outcome may be `unknown`. Missing history is not proof that no work occurred. Recovery must not simply call the command again.

The [command implementation guide](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/commands-edits) explains submission and checkpoints. The embedded example intentionally returns an uncertain result so you can see this boundary.

## Storage failure reduces recovery

Actions can still execute if storage fails. Their `recovery` state is then `unavailable`; display that limitation where a user is relying on restart recovery. `RuntimeOptions.onError` receives owner errors such as persistence failures.

## Uploads and background transfers

A command can declare a native HTTP `transfer`. With the [browser transfer host](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/browser-host#let-the-browser-continue-an-upload), the browser can accept responsibility for moving its bytes after tabs close. Without that integration, or when the browser cannot use it, the SharedWorker sends the request while the application remains open.

| Action state | What the UI can say |
| --- | --- |
| `execution.lifetime === "owner"` | Keep an application tab open; show `execution.reason` when present |
| `execution.lifetime === "browser"` | The browser accepted the transfer; closing this tab does not itself cancel it |
| `recovery === "saved"` | The action checkpoint was saved; this alone says nothing about who owns the request |

API support alone does not establish browser ownership. Vem reports `browser` only after an actual handoff acknowledgement or recovered evidence of acceptance. The browser may still stop the transfer, storage may fail, and the server may reject it. The [Background Fetch API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Background_Fetch_API) is not supported by Firefox or Safari; those browsers use the owner lifetime.

The ServiceWorker saves a bounded response receipt in the same protected journal. A returning owner uses that evidence or investigates the existing browser registration; it never starts a replacement upload. If the acknowledgement or result is missing, the outcome can remain `unknown`. A lost acknowledgement does not trigger an owner-bound fallback, because that could send the upload twice.

**Continuation is not resumption.** The journal does not contain the uploaded file, and Vem has no automatic upload replay. A resumable backend needs its own transfer identity and accepted-byte protocol. The [Background Fetch specification](https://wicg.github.io/background-fetch/) restricts automatic request restart to GET because repeating other methods can cause side effects.

The browser uses the request's credential policy; the journal does not pin a cookie, TLS identity, or authenticated session. Credentials can change while work is pending. Server authorization remains authoritative. Read-access loss removes protected activity and receipts; losing write access blocks a handoff that has not started, but does not mean already accepted work was canceled. Explicit cancellation can leave partial remote effects and must not be presented as rollback.

## One owner makes shared decisions

The SharedWorker owns acquisition, actions, and persistence. Tabs own views. A version-independent Web Lock protects ownership, including during updates. A delayed heartbeat does not authorize a second owner.

Use the [browser-host guide](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/browser-host) to configure that boundary. Reads use browser transport concurrency by default; commands remain bounded to four executions. Configure an optional read cap, command limits, and retention through [RuntimeOptions](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/reference/api/runtime.Interface.RuntimeOptions) when your backend or application needs different limits.


---

# API map

Choose the public import for the responsibility you own.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/data/reference/api-map



| Import | Audience | Main exports |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@hyecompany/vem-data` | Features and contracts | `defineResource`, `defineCommand`, `defineEdit`, `filter`, `hasFields`, descriptions and result types |
| `@hyecompany/vem-data/react` | React features | `DataProvider`, `useQuery`, `useReadStatus`, `useCommand`, `useEdit`, `useAction`, `useActivities`, `useFeedback`, `useInlineFeedback`, `queryView` |
| `@hyecompany/vem-data/client` | Tab host | `connectSharedWorker`, `BrowserClient`, compatibility |
| `@hyecompany/vem-data/worker` | Owner bootstrap | `createSharedHost`, owner contract |
| `@hyecompany/vem-data/runtime` | Domain and owner integration | `createRuntime`, `ResourceDefinition`, evidence types, `DexiePersistence` |
| `@hyecompany/vem-data/testing` | Feature tests | `createTestClient`, fixtures, `MemoryPersistence`, `deferred` |
| `@hyecompany/vem-data/devtools` | Development integration | Inspection, scenario catalog, controlled scenario client |

[Browse all generated signatures](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/reference/api), or search for an exact API name. Entry-point listings link every exported declaration, including its members and generic parameters. Shared types may be linked to their canonical declaration under another entry point.

Use only package exports. Internal stores, worker messages, and database rows are not the feature API. Low-level structural helpers `query`, `command`, and `edit` exist, but named resource contracts are the primary contributor interface.

## Upgrade from Data 1

Data 2 changes contracts implemented by custom clients, test doubles, and edit definitions. BrowserClient and the built-in runtime supply the new action controls; applications using them do not implement those methods themselves. Update the dependency and type-check your integration, including any edit definitions or handwritten test doubles.

| If you maintain… | Update for Data 2 |
| --- | --- |
| A custom `DataClient` | Support `watch(query, { acquire: false })` without adding demand, and `watchReadStatus(query)` for owner-wide matching read work. Return an `ActionObservation` from `action(id)`, including `cancel()` and `retry()`. Delegate these controls to the owner, which checks current access and admission. |
| Handwritten `EditSnapshot` objects | Supply `canEdit`: whether readable fields accept local input. It is independent of `canSave`; losing write access can still leave a locally editable draft. |
| Handwritten `TestClient` or `ScenarioFeedback` objects | Supply the feedback capability required by their public types. Prefer `createTestClient` and `createScenarioClient` instead of copying their structures. |
| Inline feedback acknowledgements | Pass the observed `phase` and, when present, `outcome.kind`. Acknowledgement needs the displayed stage, not a retained result payload. Existing typed `ActionSnapshot` values remain accepted. |
| An edit with initially absent optional fields | Declare those keys in the baseline's `fieldDisclosure`, even when `values` omits them. Fields already present in `values` inherit the baseline disclosure unless overridden. Undeclared fields can no longer be edited or saved. |

`PreparedEdit` keeps its existing shape. Its field declarations now determine which draft keys are admitted. Identity transitions and the new React feedback hooks are additive; list and detail screens keep using the same query descriptions.

Continue to [edit definitions](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/commands-edits), [feedback ownership](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/feedback), or the [generated signatures](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/reference/api) for the contract you implement.

# Troubleshooting

Start with what you see, then check the responsible layer.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/data/reference/troubleshooting


## Nothing fetched or no event socket

- **In the embedded examples:** the service is simulated inside the page. The counter measures calls to that source, not HTTP requests.
- **In your application:** inspect the existing query's `issues` and whether its requested fields and membership are already known. A satisfied query needs no acquisition. `enabled: false`, `acquire: false`, and `useReadStatus` also create no automatic acquisition.
- **With a SharedWorker host:** inspect the worker's network activity. Page developer tools may not show its requests. Your host opens the event transport; Vem does not choose or open one automatically.

A failed HTTP request is not proof of logout. Check the source URL, proxy, and authentication separately. See [when acquisition happens](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/understand/acquisition).

## Opening another task did not add a service read

The earlier response may have included both tasks' details. Vem reuses all established facts, not only those used by the first view. If it returned only one task, a missing detail on another task should cause acquisition. Check the response contents and your source declarations and response extraction before expecting one request per screen.

## Loading when changing a known filter

Check `readDefinitions` in `connectSharedWorker`: the tab needs the same pure read rules as the owner. Then check the filter fields and `confirmed.complete`. An unknown predicate or incomplete membership can require acquisition.

If the required information is present and permitted, a loading flash is a defect. Do not add a timer or a second feature cache to conceal it. [Browser setup](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/browser-host) shows the shared read definition.

## Partial rows or no confirmed total

A row's `missing` fields, unresolved filter candidates, and incomplete membership mean different things. Keep known rows visible. Only `confirmed.complete` establishes the matching set, and only `result.empty` proves emptiness. [Partial-result rendering](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/build/partial-results) provides the code.

## Read status is idle while some data is missing

`useReadStatus` observes work, not completeness. Missing notes on an offscreen task do not start a read. The component that needs notes declares a normal query; the status observer then follows matching work. Its retry only covers unsuccessful acquisition for current demands. Use a query result's `confirmed`, `unresolved`, and row fields to determine what is known. [Related read status](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/build/display#show-progress-for-related-reads).

## Save conflict

Confirm that the edit's ETag came from the same response as its baseline. Preserve the draft when the server rejects that token. Let the user reload explicitly; silently replacing the token would turn an old draft into an overwrite of someone else's changes. [Editor recipe](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/build/editors).

## Another tab has different behavior

Start with `client.connectionSnapshot()`. If it is not `ready`, address the reported connection error first. Then compare the tabs' origin, worker URL, and definitions version. Same-origin tabs must use the same ownership lock name across versions. [Host compatibility](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/browser-host#1-agree-on-compatibility).

## A failed action cannot be retried

Default retry requires a settled failure explicitly marked `submitted: false`, and excludes restored actions. A failed response after possible submission does not meet that rule. The domain can override retry only when backend evidence makes another attempt safe. [Command controls](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/build/actions).

## Data disappeared after an access change

Check whether the data lost its last allowed disclosure basis. If it did, disappearance is expected—even from an unsaved draft. Granting permission again allows new evidence; an old response cannot refill the values. [Implementing access](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/access) explains the declarations.

## Recovery is unavailable

Check `action.recovery` and the owner's `onError` reports for persistence failures. Execution can continue while restart recovery is reduced. If a command has no backend operation history to investigate, its journal cannot prove the outcome. [Recovery](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/understand/recovery).


---

# Maintainer map

Trace a documented behavior to implementation and focused tests.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/data/reference/maintainer-map



Paths below are relative to `packages/data`. Read the relevant guide first, then the implementation and behavioral tests. Internal paths are a navigation aid, not import recommendations.

| Behavior | Implementation | Test search |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typed descriptions and selected fields | `src/contracts.ts`, `src/descriptors.ts` | `tests/contracts/`, `tests/types/` |
| Query projection and partial membership | `src/read-model/`, `src/runtime/memberships.ts` | `tests/queries/`, `tests/knowledge/` |
| Missing-information acquisition | `src/runtime/acquisition.ts`, `src/runtime/planning*.ts`, `src/runtime/source-execution.ts`, `src/read-model/requirements.ts` | `tests/planning/` |
| Observations and dependencies | `src/runtime/knowledge.ts`, `src/runtime/relationships.ts` | `tests/knowledge/` |
| Access and restoration | `src/access.ts`, `src/access-proofs.ts`, `src/runtime/restoration.ts` | `tests/access/`, `tests/persistence/` |
| Actions and recovery | `src/actions.ts`, `src/actions/` | `tests/actions/`, `tests/persistence/recovery.test.ts` |
| Managed editing | `src/edit.ts`, `src/runtime/edit-admission.ts` | `tests/editing/` |
| Owner and tab publication | `src/worker.ts`, `src/client.ts`, `src/read-model/` | `tests/host/` |
| Persistence | `src/persistence.ts` | `tests/persistence/` |

The package also keeps liveness and query presentation checks in `tests/queries`, developer-tool checks in `tests/devtools`, and executable-example checks in `tests/examples`. Compile-only assertions in `tests/types/*.types.ts` run through type checking, not the runtime test runner.

At the repository root, `tests/docs` checks the built site, with focused learning tools in `tests/docs/experiments`. `tests/package` checks the actual HTTP/SharedWorker starter, including the packed independent consumer exercised by `scripts/check-package.mjs`. Helpers belong in the nearest `support` directory; only browser launch configuration shared by both suites lives in root `tests/support`.

Before changing a behavior, identify the public contract it affects and add or adjust a focused behavioral test. Keep generic owner and storage mechanics out of domain-specific feature additions.

## Trace a query update

The owner publishes permitted records and membership evidence. A tab applies that publication to its local read model and projects the queries its components use. The owner uses the same projection rules when deciding what information is still missing. Feature code does not manage either copy.

For an existing query, Vem retains each record's contribution: whether it matches, its displayed values, and its missing requirements. A record update recalculates that record's contribution. Unchanged records reuse their previous calculations. Custom scope and filter functions are evaluated again for a changed record; Vem does not assume that these functions read only selected fields.

Before projection, an ordinary observation recalculates currency for changed facts and facts whose evidence depends on them. The dependency index carries changes through derived facts and relationships; it does not treat a new value as evidence that unrelated facts changed. Access changes and event-continuity changes can require broader checks.

This saves repeated evaluation of every resource when one resource changes. Assembling a changed result can still depend on its row count. It is not a constant-time guarantee for every publication.

Access and membership changes can affect which records belong or may be disclosed, so they require broader recomputation. Initial attachment, reset, or a query falling behind the bounded change history can also rebuild its projection. These paths preserve the same results as a full calculation. Inactive retained queries do not perform notification work; reading them again catches up to the current model.

Start with `src/read-model/query-projector.ts` for query contributions, `src/read-model/projection.ts` for the tab's local model, and `src/runtime/read-model-export.ts` plus `src/read-model/publication.ts` for publication changes. Follow the behavior tests in `tests/host` and `tests/queries` before changing their bookkeeping.

## Measure the right work

Run from the repository root:

```sh
node --import tsx scripts/benchmarks/data-publication.mjs 100 1000 5000
node --import tsx scripts/benchmarks/publication-pipeline.mjs 100 1000 5000
```

The first isolates owner observation without active owner queries and tab projection. The second includes active owner queries and three simulated tabs, measuring delta preparation, structured cloning, replica application, and subscriber reads separately. It checks selected-field updates, movement between filters, and updates outside some selections.

These are CPU benchmarks with deterministic data. Their sum is not browser interaction latency: actual Worker scheduling, network, React, and rendering are excluded. Use a browser profile to assess those parts, and behavioral tests to assert which records are evaluated rather than machine-specific timing limits. `packages/data/tests/README.md` documents the benchmark settings and comparison options.


---

# Integration limits

Know which guarantees your backend and browser host must provide.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/data/reference/limits


## Bound requests that may never return

Vem settles an acquisition when the source answers or fails. The runtime currently has no built-in deadline for a source promise that never settles. This is a gap in the intended finite-read guarantee: a hanging adapter can keep an imperative read pending.

Set transport deadlines in your domain integration. An imperative caller can also bound its own wait:


```ts
import type { DataClient } from "@hyecompany/vem-data";
import { firstTask, tasks } from "../task-board/contract.js";
export function readTaskWithDeadline(client: DataClient) {
	return client.read(tasks.get(firstTask, { select: ["title"] }), {
		signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000),
	});
}
```


`DataClient` comes from `@hyecompany/vem-data`; `tasks` is the application's resource contract. Catch an aborted read at the caller. Aborting withdraws that caller's demand, including reads queued before attachment. It does not cancel shared work needed by another view. An acquisition already in flight may finish and contribute permitted evidence; the abandoned reader does not request further acquisition.

## Automatic planning is bounded

Vem chooses acquisition sets from declared capabilities and current knowledge. It cannot infer undocumented backend semantics or know future demand. When record identities or related links are unknown, it may first acquire membership, then plan again with that evidence. Its default policy uses observed population and response shape; unknown size stays unknown. Optional backend cost estimates must be justified by the integration. The bounded search keeps the best plan it finds, not a universal optimum.

Reads have no default concurrency cap: Vem combines demand and forwards fetch-priority hints to the browser. A host may set `maxConcurrent` for a backend with a specific concurrency constraint. `maxAcquisitionsPerRead` defaults to 4,096 dispatched sources per attempt; exhausting it leaves a partial result with an explanation. Paged sources default to at most 100 pages unless configured. Sources must provide transport deadlines and truthful completeness. These bounds prevent an unbounded acquisition loop; increase them deliberately for larger supported workloads.

## Match promises to your integration

| You want… | Your integration must provide… |
| --- | --- |
| Current data after a disconnected event stream | Accurate field/channel continuity and replay or reacquisition after a gap |
| Private fields to disappear on access loss | Accurate access decisions and disclosure bases |
| Conditional saves | A token from the same writable representation as the draft baseline |
| Recovery after the owner stops | Persistence plus backend evidence the domain can investigate |
| An upload that continues after tabs close | The [browser transfer host](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/browser-host#let-the-browser-continue-an-upload), durable storage, browser support, and confirmed handoff |
| A resumable transfer | A backend transfer protocol and enough durable metadata to resume it |
| Form-library values to be forgotten | Integration that withdraws its values and defaults alongside the edit session |

Vem provides the coordination contracts. It does not generate backend semantics from a schema or supply a form library, authorization server, upload protocol, or development panel.

## What the documentation examples exercise

The embedded examples run Vem against simulated services in the page. They demonstrate shared planning, per-field continuity, actions, access, and edits. Their counters do not represent HTTP traffic; their recovery example uses memory storage.

Repository integration checks separately exercise an actual SharedWorker, HTTP/events, conditional writes, and a packed independent consumer. Backend-specific behaviors still belong in your domain's tests. Use [feature fixtures](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/build/testing) for screens and [the resource guide](https://hyevem.com/docs/data/connect/resources) for integration boundaries.


---

# Contribute to these docs

Keep guides, examples, reference, and exports in sync.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/data/reference/contributing



## Update a guide

Edit `packages/docs/content/handbook`. Lead with the task and prerequisites, show a small useful example, explain the decisions the reader must make, and link a relevant next step. Add a page's title, description, and order in frontmatter. Navigation and machine-readable exports are generated from that content.

Run `npm run docs:prepare` after content changes, then `npm run docs:dev` to preview. Generated content in `content/docs`, `.generated`, and the static `out` artifact is not edited by hand. Source typechecking excludes the previous `out` artifact; the actual example files are compiled separately. During a running preview, rerun `docs:prepare` to publish source changes.

## Show executable code

Put runnable TypeScript in `packages/<package>/examples`, imported only through public package entries. Keep generic examples framework-neutral; Next.js client boundaries belong in the documentation preview wrapper or a specifically labeled Next.js example. Mark a focused region with `// #region name` and `// #endregion name`. Use an `Example` include with its file and optional region in a guide. The default package is Data; add `package="ui"` for UI snippets. The generator inserts that exact code. Include the code needed for the task on the page; a source link should never be required to understand an omitted step.

Compile examples with `npm run typecheck`. Add negative type assertions for important boundaries such as unselected fields, invalid command inputs, and proposal targets. Do not maintain a second hand-copied tutorial implementation.

## Add a diagram or experiment

Diagram content lives in `content/diagrams.json`. Each node keeps its title, icon, color, and short explanation together. Static diagrams should explain the whole relationship at a glance. Use interaction only when changing something teaches a behavior that a static picture cannot. Add an icon to the small map in `components/Flow.tsx` when needed.

Experiment prompts and explanations live in `content/experiments.json`; focused implementations live in `components/labs`. Start with one useful move the reader can make, then make its result easy to see. Keep technical scope and longer explanations in the expandable section.

The task board at `components/TaskBoardDemo.tsx` is a short, ordered walkthrough of the same lessons used in the guides. `components/lesson` owns the shared application view and teaching presentation, using public Vem UI components. `components/labs/sources` owns each controlled source. Both use public Vem APIs.

Give each lesson one familiar task first. Explain the observed result in one sentence, after the interaction. Keep unusual responses and permission changes in optional controls. Teach with the app, not a panel of internal state. Match the guide’s technical explanation to that experience, and verify the initial state as well as the failure paths.

Tutorial snippets are extracted from compiled files in `packages/data/examples`. Keep each excerpt focused, and show or explain the imports and local values it needs. The repository fixture separately checks HTTP and SharedWorker integration; running it is a contributor check, not a reader prerequisite. The in-page lessons use simulated calls, so never label their counters as HTTP traffic.

Each experiment needs an initial state, a few labeled controls, reset, observable results, and honest execution scope. Keep interaction user-controlled and keyboard accessible. Add browser checks for reset and meaningful failure paths. Avoid one combined control panel that requires learning every concept at once.

## Document a UI component

Add its guide and compiled example, then register the public exports in `content/ui-components.json`. The catalog, search, and text exports come from that metadata and guide. `ComponentPreview` renders the same example used by the guide; give it a clear initial state and reset. Keep Data bindings alongside the other components, with their provider prerequisites on the guide.

Use `UiReference` with the public symbol name to generate a link to its exact TypeDoc page and props. Do not copy prop tables or import internal package files. Retired URLs belong in the static redirect map in `packages/docs/scripts/finalize-export.mjs`.

## Change the API reference

Update JSDoc on the public source declaration. `scripts/generate-reference.mjs` reads each documented package's public JavaScript export entry points through pinned TypeDoc and its Markdown plugin. The package map in `scripts/documented-packages.mjs` assigns reference output locations without changing published Data URLs. Stylesheet exports stay in the usage guides. Signatures and member lists are generated; semantic responsibilities belong in source comments and the relevant guide.

## Review the teaching value

Read the rendered page as someone doing the task for the first time. Can they tell where the code belongs, understand its inputs, and use its output without opening a source repository? Explain one practical default before introducing optional mechanisms. Remove repeated scope disclaimers, unexplained API lists, and controls that do not teach anything new.

## Validate the reader journeys

```sh
npm run check
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run test:package
npm run docs:build
npm run test:docs
```

For Pages, build with `BASE_PATH=/vem-web` in the environment. Check search, links and anchors, mobile width, zoom, keyboard focus, reduced motion, and ordinary reading with JavaScript disabled. Do not publish as a side effect of local validation.

`llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, and `docs.json` come from the same content. Text exports expand code excerpts and explain diagrams and experiments; they must not contain unresolved component tags.

For host development, `npm run example:dev` starts the repository's HTTP/event fixture and SharedWorker application on `http://127.0.0.1:4310`. Use it to investigate transport or cross-tab behavior. The learning examples remain embedded in the docs.


---

# Vem UI

React components with a consistent design, shared updates, and application-owned branding.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/ui


Vem UI provides controls, navigation, and feedback for React applications. Install one package and receive component fixes through ordinary package updates. Your application keeps its router, content, and layouts.

## Add the package

Use React 19 and React DOM 19:

```sh
npm install @hyecompany/vem-ui
```

Include `@hyecompany/vem-ui/styles.css` once at your application entry. The package ships its own CSS; Tailwind and shadcn source installation are not required.


```tsx
import { Button } from "@hyecompany/vem-ui";
import "@hyecompany/vem-ui/styles.css";

export function App() {
	return <Button>New task</Button>;
}
```


<details>
<summary>Using Next.js</summary>

The examples are ordinary React. In Next.js, put a `"use client"` boundary around your application components that use state, event handlers, or browser APIs. Import the stylesheet in the root layout. Vite and other client applications do not need that directive.

</details>

## Choose what to build

| Your task | Go here |
| --- | --- |
| Add a control or navigation | [Components](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components) |
| Match the application's appearance | [Branding and appearance](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/customize) |
| Connect a Data query, command, or edit | [Use Vem UI with Data](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/with-data) |
| Look up props | [API reference](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference) |

The [task board](https://hyevem.com/docs/task-board) uses these same public components with Vem Data.

## Update the package

Use your package manager to update the dependency and review the release notes. Component implementation stays in Vem; application branding stays in your stylesheet. There are no copied registry files to merge.

The controls use shadcn’s Base UI composition and Nova styling, with ordinary semantic CSS variables for [application branding](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/customize). Existing theme variables are respected through CSS; build-time `components.json` settings are not read by an installed npm package.

# Button

Run an action.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/button


Import from `@hyecompany/vem-ui` after [adding the package](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui#add-the-package).

### Preview: Button

Run an action with clear emphasis. The example uses the public package component. Reset restores its initial state.

## Use it


```tsx
import { Button } from "@hyecompany/vem-ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export function ButtonExample() {
	const [saved, setSaved] = useState(false);
	return (
		<div
			style={{
				display: "flex",
				gap: "0.75rem",
				alignItems: "center",
				flexWrap: "wrap",
			}}
		>
			<Button variant="default" onClick={() => setSaved(true)}>
				Save task
			</Button>
			<Button variant="ghost" onClick={() => setSaved(false)}>
				Undo
			</Button>
			<output aria-live="polite">
				{saved ? "Task saved" : "Ready to save"}
			</output>
		</div>
	);
}
```


## Behavior and choices

Use `variant="default"` for the primary action, `outline` or `secondary` for alternatives, and `ghost` for a quiet control. `destructive` and `link` are also available. Sizes are `default`, `xs`, `sm`, `lg`, and the matching `icon` sizes.

Use `disabled` when an action cannot be attempted. For progress, include [Spinner](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/spinner) and a readable label; `aria-busy` communicates that the control is working. Give icon-only buttons an accessible name.

Button renders a button by default. Its `render` prop composes another element while keeping button interaction semantics; it is not a navigation-link abstraction. Use a real link for navigation, such as a router link composed through SidebarMenuButton or BreadcrumbLink. Set `type="submit"` when submitting a form.

[API reference](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.Function.Button)


---

# Input

Collect a short text value.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/input


Import from `@hyecompany/vem-ui` after [adding the package](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui#add-the-package).

### Preview: Input

Collect a short text value. The example uses the public package component. Reset restores its initial state.

## Use it


```tsx
import { Input } from "@hyecompany/vem-ui";
import { useId } from "react";

export function InputExample() {
	const id = useId();
	return (
		<label htmlFor={id}>
			Task title
			<Input id={id} name="title" defaultValue="Plan a weekend walk" />
		</label>
	);
}
```


## Behavior and choices

Use native input props for type, validation, autofill, and form submission. Associate a visible label with `id`. A placeholder is a hint, not a label.

For related controls, compose Input and Button in your own form layout. Use `aria-describedby` to connect a hint or validation message; set `aria-invalid` only when a value has been found invalid.

[API reference](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.Function.Input)

# Textarea

Edit a longer text value.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/textarea


Import from `@hyecompany/vem-ui` after [adding the package](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui#add-the-package).

### Preview: Textarea

Edit a longer text value. The example uses the public package component. Reset restores its initial state.

## Use it


```tsx
import { Textarea } from "@hyecompany/vem-ui";
import { useId } from "react";

export function TextareaExample() {
	const id = useId();
	return (
		<label htmlFor={id}>
			Notes
			<Textarea
				id={id}
				name="notes"
				defaultValue="Meet by the lake at 10."

		</label>

}
```


## Behavior and choices

Use native textarea props, including `rows`, `required`, and `maxLength`. Keep its visible label even when the field has a placeholder.

For protected Vem Data drafts, use [managed text bindings](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/data-bindings); an independent `useState` copy cannot follow selective disclosure withdrawal.

[API reference](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.Function.Textarea)

# Switch

Toggle a setting immediately.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/switch


Import from `@hyecompany/vem-ui` after [adding the package](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui#add-the-package).

### Preview: Switch

Toggle a setting immediately. The example uses the public package component. Reset restores its initial state.

## Use it


```tsx
import { Switch } from "@hyecompany/vem-ui";
import { useId, useState } from "react";

export function SwitchExample() {
	const id = useId();
	const [enabled, setEnabled] = useState(false);
	return (
		<div style={{ display: "flex", gap: "0.75rem", alignItems: "center" }}>
			<Switch id={id} checked={enabled} onCheckedChange={setEnabled} />
			<label htmlFor={id}>Show completed tasks</label>
		</div>
	);
}
```


## Behavior and choices

Use a switch for an on/off setting. `checked` and `onCheckedChange` give controlled behavior; `defaultChecked` gives an initial uncontrolled value. Native `name` and `value` participate in form submission.

The visible label describes the setting, not the next action. Keyboard users can focus it and press Space. Use `disabled` only when the setting cannot be changed.

[API reference](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.Function.Switch)


---

# Tabs

Switch between related views without navigation.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/tabs


Import from `@hyecompany/vem-ui` after [adding the package](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui#add-the-package).

### Preview: Tabs

Switch between related views without navigation. The example uses the public package component. Reset restores its initial state.

## Use it


```tsx
import { Tabs, TabsContent, TabsList, TabsTrigger } from "@hyecompany/vem-ui";

export function TabsExample() {
	return (
		<Tabs defaultValue="todo">
			<TabsList activateOnFocus aria-label="Tasks">
				<TabsTrigger value="todo">To do</TabsTrigger>
				<TabsTrigger value="done">Done</TabsTrigger>
			</TabsList>
			<TabsContent value="todo">Plan a weekend walk</TabsContent>
			<TabsContent value="done">Check the forecast</TabsContent>
		</Tabs>
	);
}
```


## Behavior and choices

Pair each trigger and panel with the same `value`. Use `defaultValue` for a local selection or `value` and `onValueChange` for controlled state. Label the tab list. Arrow keys move focus between tabs. This example uses `activateOnFocus` to open a tab immediately; without it, Enter or Space activates the focused tab. Tab continues into the active panel.

Inactive content unmounts by default. Use `keepMounted` on a panel only when that lifetime is intentional: hidden Data consumers still express demand. Use links and [Sidebar](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/sidebar) for application routes.

[API reference](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.Function.Tabs)


---

Add a short status label.

import { Badge } from "@hyecompany/vem-ui";

export function BadgeExample() {

Use `variant="secondary"` for supporting labels, `outline` for a bordered label, or `destructive` for an error. The default variant uses the primary color. Always include readable text; color alone does not communicate status.

# Card

Group a small piece of related content.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/card


Import from `@hyecompany/vem-ui` after [adding the package](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui#add-the-package).

## Preview

### Preview: Card

Group a small piece of related content. The example uses the public package component. Reset restores its initial state.

## Use it


```tsx
import {
	Card,
	CardContent,
	CardDescription,
	CardHeader,
	CardTitle,
} from "@hyecompany/vem-ui";

export function CardExample() {
	return (
		<Card>
			<CardHeader>
				<CardTitle>
					<h3>Weekend plans</h3>
				</CardTitle>
				<CardDescription>A little time outdoors.</CardDescription>
			</CardHeader>
			<CardContent>Plan a walk and pack a picnic.</CardContent>

}
```


## Behavior and choices

Compose the parts you need; a card does not fetch data or make itself clickable. CardTitle is a styled container; place an appropriately ranked heading inside when the content needs one. CardAction puts a control beside the header.

Keep the action as a real button or link inside the card. Use your own layout around cards rather than teaching the component about application grids.

[API reference](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.Function.Card)

# Separator

Visually separate adjacent groups.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/separator


Import from `@hyecompany/vem-ui` after [adding the package](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui#add-the-package).

Visually separate adjacent groups. The example uses the public package component. Reset restores its initial state.

## Use it


```tsx
import { Separator } from "@hyecompany/vem-ui";

export function SeparatorExample() {
	return (
		<div>
			<p>Weekend plans</p>
			<Separator />
			<p>Two tasks to do</p>
		</div>
	);
}
```


## Behavior and choices

The separator is exposed to assistive technology. Use `aria-hidden="true"` for a purely decorative divider. `orientation="vertical"` creates a vertical divider; its parent provides the available height.

A heading is usually clearer than a divider when introducing a new section.

# Tooltip

Repeat a visual label on hover or focus.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/tooltip


Import from `@hyecompany/vem-ui` after [adding the package](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui#add-the-package).

### Preview: Tooltip

Repeat a visual label on hover or focus. The example uses the public package component. Reset restores its initial state.

## Use it


```tsx
import {
	Button,
	Tooltip,
	TooltipContent,
	TooltipProvider,
	TooltipTrigger,
} from "@hyecompany/vem-ui";

export function TooltipExample() {
	return (
		<TooltipProvider>
			<Tooltip>
				<TooltipTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>
					Save task
				</TooltipTrigger>
				<TooltipContent>Keep the changes to this task.</TooltipContent>
			</Tooltip>
		</TooltipProvider>
	);
}
```


## Behavior and choices

Put TooltipTrigger and TooltipContent inside Tooltip. `render` gives the trigger the semantics and styling of your existing control. TooltipProvider supplies shared delay settings; place it around a related group when needed.

The tooltip is a visual label, not an accessible description relationship. Keep the trigger’s accessible name and all essential instructions on the control or inline in the page. It may not be available to touch users. Use a dialog or other appropriate disclosure for additional interactive content.

[API reference](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.Function.Tooltip)


---

# Combobox

Choose a value from a searchable list.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/combobox


Import from `@hyecompany/vem-ui` after [adding the package](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui#add-the-package).

### Preview: Combobox

Choose a value from a searchable list. The example uses the public package component. Reset restores its initial state.

## Use it


```tsx
import {
	Combobox,
	ComboboxContent,
	ComboboxEmpty,
	ComboboxInput,
	ComboboxItem,
	ComboboxList,
} from "@hyecompany/vem-ui";
import { useId, useState } from "react";

const boards = ["Weekend", "Work", "São Paulo"];

export function ComboboxExample() {
	const id = useId();
	const [board, setBoard] = useState<string | null>("Weekend");
	return (
		<div style={{ maxWidth: "20rem" }}>
			<label htmlFor={id}>Choose a board</label>
			<Combobox items={boards} value={board} onValueChange={setBoard}>
				<ComboboxInput id={id} placeholder="Search boards…" />
				<ComboboxContent>
					<ComboboxEmpty>No matching boards.</ComboboxEmpty>
					<ComboboxList>
						{(item: string) => (
							<ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>
								{item}
							</ComboboxItem>
						)}
					</ComboboxList>
				</ComboboxContent>
			</Combobox>
		</div>
	);
}
```


## Behavior and choices

`items` describes the available choices. ComboboxInput supplies the editable search field; ComboboxList renders the matching options. Selecting an option changes `value`; typing changes the search text, not the selected value. On opening, the selected option is highlighted. `autoHighlight` controls highlighting matches while filtering; it does not disable that selected-option behavior.

The built-in filter matches text locally. Pass `filter` when the domain needs a different matching rule, or `filter={null}` when your source has already filtered the results. The component does not fetch data. Keep source demand in your data integration and loading, error, and retry content outside the options list.

Object values can supply `itemToStringLabel` and `itemToStringValue`. Use `multiple` with ComboboxChips, ComboboxChip, and ComboboxChipsInput for several selections. Grouped choices use ComboboxGroup, ComboboxLabel, and ComboboxCollection.

Both list variants retain a thin native scrollbar when content overflows, following the browser and operating system’s visibility preferences.

ComboboxContent opens in a portal. It inherits document-level CSS variables; use its `container` prop for an intentionally scoped theme. Give the input a visible label and preserve keyboard selection and Escape dismissal.

[API reference](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.Function.Combobox)

Use `indicatorSide="end"` on ComboboxItem to place its selection checkmark after the label. The default is `"start"`.

ComboboxList gently introduces new options and moves remaining options as matches change. Removed options leave the DOM immediately; selection and keyboard navigation always use the current list. The popup smoothly resizes as options or status content change, including when options disappear. `--vem-combobox-duration` (160ms) and `--vem-combobox-easing` coordinate opening and size changes; use the same variables for an application trigger that expands. Motion is disabled for reduced-motion preferences; lists with more than 100 rendered options skip individual row motion. Keep item keys stable so the same option retains its identity while filtering or receiving new data.


## With Vem Data

Use [useSearch](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/data-bindings#search-shared-information) to connect typed text to a query predicate. Bind its `value` to `inputValue` and call `setValue` from `onInputValueChange` for text edits. Pass the query's rows as the choices and `filter={null}` so Combobox does not apply a second matching rule. Keep the selected identity separate from the search text.

Pass `{ enabled: open }` to release this query's demand while the popup is closed. Clear transient text with `setValue("")` on close. Render [QueryStatus](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/query-status) outside ComboboxList so loading, incomplete results, and retry remain separate from selectable options.

## Large choice lists

Set `virtualized` on Combobox and replace ComboboxList with ComboboxVirtualList. Keep the full choice collection at the root: keyboard navigation and search must know about choices that have not mounted. The virtual list owns scrolling, measurement, and accessible option positions.


```tsx
import {
	Combobox,
	ComboboxContent,
	ComboboxEmpty,
	ComboboxInput,
	ComboboxItem,
	ComboboxVirtualList,
} from "@hyecompany/vem-ui";

interface Board {
	id: string;
	name: string;
}
export function LargeBoardSelector({ boards }: { boards: readonly Board[] }) {
	return (
		<Combobox
			virtualized
			items={boards}
			itemToStringLabel={(board: Board) => board.name}
			isItemEqualToValue={(left, right) => left.id === right.id}
		>
			<ComboboxInput aria-label="Board" placeholder="Search boards…" />
			<ComboboxContent>
				<ComboboxEmpty>No matching boards.</ComboboxEmpty>
				<ComboboxVirtualList<Board> getItemKey={(board) => board.id}>
					{(board) => <ComboboxItem value={board}>{board.name}</ComboboxItem>}
				</ComboboxVirtualList>
			</ComboboxContent>
		</Combobox>
	);
}
```


The callback also receives `{ visible, index }`. Enable optional detail queries only when `visible` is true; overscan and the highlighted offscreen option do not create demand. A changing description can change row height without overlapping its neighbors. The component does not fetch data itself.

Use stable keys and flat choices. Keep `virtualized` enabled for the mounted combobox; the same component handles both short and long lists. Search resets the scroll position, keyboard navigation reaches unmounted choices, and pointer hover does not move the viewport. Keep status and retry controls outside this listbox. For non-selectable content, use [VirtualList](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/virtual-list).

[API reference](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.Function.ComboboxVirtualList) · [All props](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.TypeAlias.ComboboxVirtualListProps)


---

# Sidebar

Compose application navigation and a mobile drawer.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/sidebar


Import from `@hyecompany/vem-ui` after [adding the package](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui#add-the-package).

### Preview: Sidebar

Provide desktop navigation and a mobile drawer. The example uses the public package component. Reset restores its initial state.

## Use it

The preview uses SidebarNavigation inside the Sidebar frame. Place your navigation and page content in an application shell:


```tsx
import {
	Sidebar,
	SidebarContent,
	SidebarHeader,
	SidebarInset,
	SidebarProvider,
	SidebarTrigger,
} from "@hyecompany/vem-ui";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";

export function AppShell({
	navigation,
	children,
}: {
	navigation: ReactNode;
	children: ReactNode;
}) {
	return (
		<SidebarProvider>
			<Sidebar>
				<SidebarHeader>Weekend</SidebarHeader>
				<SidebarContent>{navigation}</SidebarContent>
			</Sidebar>
			<SidebarInset>
				<header>
					<SidebarTrigger aria-label="Toggle navigation" />
				</header>
				{children}
			</SidebarInset>
		</SidebarProvider>
	);
}
```


## Add destinations

SidebarNavigation composes links and nested destinations with the same sidebar interaction. Give each item a stable key, label, and native or router link through `render`. Optional `icon` content appears before the label. Set `isActive` from your router; Vem applies current-page semantics and styling. The application retains destination and route matching decisions.


```tsx
import { SidebarNavigation } from "@hyecompany/vem-ui";

export function BoardNavigation() {
	return (
		<SidebarNavigation
			aria-label="Board"
			items={[
				{
					key: "plans",
					label: "Plans",
					render: <a href="#plans">Plans</a>,
					children: [
						{
							key: "walk",
							label: "Weekend walk",
							render: <a href="#walk">Weekend walk</a>,
						},
						{
							key: "picnic",
							label: "Picnic",
							render: <a href="#picnic">Picnic</a>,
						},
					],
				},
				{
					key: "completed",
					label: "Completed",
					render: <a href="#completed">Completed</a>,
				},
			]}
		/>
	);
}
```


Place it inside SidebarProvider and a Sidebar section. It closes the mobile drawer when a destination is activated. A parent with `children` keeps navigation separate from disclosure: its label follows its link and its disclosure control expands the children. In compact desktop mode, hover previews a flyout; mouse click and Enter navigate, while touch, Space, and arrows open the flyout. Supply `container` only when flyouts need a scoped portal theme.

## Behavior and choices

For an application shell, place Sidebar and SidebarInset inside SidebarProvider, with SidebarTrigger in a reachable header. The sidebar supplies responsive presentation; your router supplies links and the active route. Use SidebarMenuButton’s `render` prop to compose your router link and `isActive` for its selected styling. Set `aria-current="page"` on the current route link.

This embedded preview uses `collapsible="none"` so it stays inside the page. Application sidebars can use `collapsible="offcanvas"` (the default) or `"icon"`. Keep labels or tooltips available when collapsed.

SidebarGroup, SidebarMenu, and SidebarMenuSub compose sections and nested links without a fixed application navigation schema. Header, footer, input, badge, skeleton, separator, and action parts share the same styles.

`useSidebar()` exposes the current state and toggle function to custom controls inside SidebarProvider. Use controlled `open` and `onOpenChange` when the application owns expanded state. The mobile drawer manages focus and dismissal separately; keep a visible trigger available.

## Compose a custom branch

Place PlanLinks inside SidebarMenu. The trigger uses `role="link"` to retain navigation semantics when it is composed into the compact-mode menu trigger. SidebarMenuBranch keeps navigation separate from disclosure: the parent label follows its link, while a separate control expands its children. In a collapsed desktop sidebar, it presents the same links in a flyout. `open`, `defaultOpen`, and `onOpenChange` control expansion; `container` supports an intentionally scoped portal theme.


```tsx
import {
	SidebarMenuBranch,
	SidebarMenuButton,
	SidebarMenuItem,
	SidebarMenuSub,
	SidebarMenuSubButton,
	SidebarMenuSubItem,
} from "@hyecompany/vem-ui";

export function PlanLinks() {
	return (
		<SidebarMenuItem>
			<SidebarMenuBranch
				label="Plans"
				trigger={
					<SidebarMenuButton
						role="link"
						isActive
						render={
							<a href="#plans" aria-current="page">
								<span>Plans</span>
							</a>
						}
					/>
				}
			>
				<SidebarMenuSub>
					<SidebarMenuSubItem>
						<SidebarMenuSubButton render={<a href="#walk">Weekend walk</a>} />
					</SidebarMenuSubItem>
					<SidebarMenuSubItem>
						<SidebarMenuSubButton render={<a href="#picnic">Picnic</a>} />
					</SidebarMenuSubItem>
				</SidebarMenuSub>
			</SidebarMenuBranch>
		</SidebarMenuItem>
	);
}
```


The children remain ordinary SidebarMenuSub, SidebarMenuSubItem, and SidebarMenuSubButton elements. Your router and link components remain responsible for destinations and current-route state.

[API reference](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.Function.SidebarNavigation) · [All props](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.Interface.SidebarNavigationProps) · [API reference](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.Function.SidebarProvider) · [API reference](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.Function.SidebarMenuBranch) · [All props](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.Interface.SidebarMenuBranchProps)

# Virtual list

Keep long lists responsive while rows grow and shrink.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/virtual-list


VirtualList renders the rows near its viewport instead of mounting the whole collection. Scroll through these tasks, then show their notes: visible rows are measured as their content changes.

### Preview: Virtual list

Render long lists with measured, changing row heights. The example uses the public package component. Reset restores its initial state.

## Use it

Import `VirtualList` from `@hyecompany/vem-ui` after [adding the package](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui#add-the-package). Supply stable unique keys and a maximum height. The list uses a 32px estimate until each row is measured; choose `estimateItemHeight` when your rows are usually taller.


```tsx
interface Task {
	id: string;
	name: string;
	notes: string;
}
export function TaskList({
	tasks,
	showNotes,
}: {
	tasks: readonly Task[];
	showNotes: boolean;
}) {
	return (
		<VirtualList
			items={tasks}
			getItemKey={(task) => task.id}
			aria-label="Tasks"
			style={{ maxHeight: 240 }}
		>
			{(task) => (
				<article
					style={{
						padding: "8px 12px",
						borderBottom: "1px solid var(--border)",
					}}
				>
					<strong>{task.name}</strong>
					{showNotes && (
						<p style={{ margin: "4px 0 0", color: "var(--muted-foreground)" }}>
							{task.notes}
						</p>
					)}
				</article>
			)}
		</VirtualList>
	);
}
```


Use [ComboboxVirtualList](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/combobox#large-choice-lists) for selectable choices. It adds the keyboard and active-option behavior a plain list does not supply.

## Load details for visible rows

The render callback also receives `{ index, visible }`. `visible` is true when the row intersects the list viewport. Nearby rows rendered as overscan have `visible=false`. Use this distinction to enable a row's detail query only while needed; keep known collection identities available for filtering and navigation.

VirtualList does not fetch or retain row data. Offscreen rows retain measured sizes; readable content, access withdrawal, and acquisition still belong to the data layer. An active descendant can stay mounted outside the viewport through `activeIndex`, without becoming visible.

## Sizing and motion

`overscan` defaults to 3 extra rows on each side; use 0 when no offscreen rendering is wanted. Rows and the viewport respond to resizing. Newly added identities appear gently, and content-height changes animate unless reduced motion is preferred. Scrolling existing identities does not trigger entry animations. Removed items leave immediately; surviving rows move into their new positions without preserving removed content.

The default maximum height is 20rem. Override it with `style` or `className`. `actionsRef` supplies `scrollToIndex` and `scrollToKey` for explicit navigation; scrolling is immediate so measurement changes can settle accurately. Use `initialIndex` to reveal a row on the first mount. The component forwards its ordinary `ref` to the scroll container.

This is a single vertical list, not a table or grid virtualizer. Browser Find searches mounted rows only. Use a normal list for short content or when searching every rendered word is more useful than virtualization.

[API reference](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.Function.VirtualList) · [All props](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.Interface.VirtualListProps)


---

# Breadcrumb

Show a page’s place in a hierarchy.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/breadcrumb


Import from `@hyecompany/vem-ui` after [adding the package](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui#add-the-package).

### Preview: Breadcrumb

Show a page’s place in a hierarchy. The example uses the public package component. Reset restores its initial state.

## Use it


```tsx
import {
	Breadcrumb,
	BreadcrumbItem,
	BreadcrumbLink,
	BreadcrumbList,
	BreadcrumbPage,
	BreadcrumbSeparator,
} from "@hyecompany/vem-ui";

export function BreadcrumbExample() {
	return (
		<Breadcrumb id="weekend">
			<BreadcrumbList>
				<BreadcrumbItem>
					<BreadcrumbLink href="#weekend">Weekend</BreadcrumbLink>
				</BreadcrumbItem>
				<BreadcrumbSeparator />
				<BreadcrumbItem>
					<BreadcrumbPage>Plan a walk</BreadcrumbPage>
				</BreadcrumbItem>
			</BreadcrumbList>
		</Breadcrumb>
	);
}
```


## Behavior and choices

Use links for ancestors and BreadcrumbPage for the current page. Separators are decorative. The default navigation label is “breadcrumb”; provide a more specific label when necessary.

BreadcrumbLink accepts a normal `href`. Its `render` prop can compose with a router link without nesting interactive elements.

[API reference](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.Function.Breadcrumb)

# Toasts

Show brief feedback away from a control.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/toast


Import from `@hyecompany/vem-ui` after [adding the package](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui#add-the-package).

### Preview: Toasts

Show brief application feedback away from a control. The example uses the public package component. Reset restores its initial state.

## Use it


```tsx
import { Button, createToastManager, Toaster } from "@hyecompany/vem-ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export function ToastExample() {
	const [manager] = useState(() => createToastManager());
	return (
		<Toaster toastManager={manager}>
			<Button
				onClick={() =>
					manager.add({
						title: "Task saved",
						description: "Your changes are ready.",
						type: "success",
					})
				}
			>
				Save task
			</Button>
		</Toaster>
	);
}
```


## Behavior and choices

Mount Toaster once around the part of your application that produces notifications. `toast.add({ title, description, type })` uses the shared manager; `createToastManager()` provides an isolated manager, as in this example. `useToastManager()` reads the nearest provider.

Use `type` for `success`, `error`, `warning`, `info`, or `loading` feedback. Set `timeout: 0` when a message must stay until dismissed. Use the returned ID with `update` or `close`. Put required decisions and detailed errors near the affected content rather than relying on a transient toast.

For a custom presentation, compose ToastProvider, ToastPortal, ToastViewport, Toast, ToastContent, ToastTitle, ToastDescription, ToastAction, and ToastClose. [ActivityToasts](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/activity-toasts) connects this presentation to Vem Data’s shared feedback ownership.

[API reference](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.Function.Toaster)

# Input group

Combine an input with supporting text or actions.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/input-group


Import from `@hyecompany/vem-ui` after [adding the package](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui#add-the-package).

### Preview: Input group

Combine an input with supporting text or actions. The example uses the public package component. Reset restores its initial state.

## Use it


```tsx
import {
	InputGroup,
	InputGroupAddon,
	InputGroupInput,
	InputGroupText,
} from "@hyecompany/vem-ui";
import { useId } from "react";
export function InputGroupExample() {
	const id = useId();
	return (
		<div style={{ maxWidth: "22rem" }}>
			<label htmlFor={id}>Board address</label>
			<InputGroup>
				<InputGroupAddon>
					<InputGroupText>tasks.example/</InputGroupText>
				</InputGroupAddon>
				<InputGroupInput id={id} defaultValue="weekend" />
			</InputGroup>
		</div>
	);
}
```


## Behavior and choices

InputGroup groups a control with InputGroupAddon content. Use InputGroupInput or InputGroupTextarea for the editable value. Supporting text uses InputGroupText, and a nearby action uses InputGroupButton.

Keep a visible label associated with the input. A prefix is context, not its accessible name. The addon’s `align` chooses `inline-start`, `inline-end`, `block-start`, or `block-end`.

[API reference](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.Function.InputGroup)

# OverflowText

Keep long names readable in compact buttons and list items.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/overflow-text


Give the component its full text and a container with a constrained width. It shortens the visible label when needed and can reveal the rest on hover or focus.

### Preview: A long project name

The label fits a narrow control. Hover or focus the control to reveal the end of its name. Change the width to see it measure the available space. The full name is also written beneath the control, so reading it never requires animation.

## Put a label in a fixed space

[Add the package](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui#add-the-package) first. Import its components and include the stylesheet once:


```tsx
import { OverflowText, Spinner } from "@hyecompany/vem-ui";
import "@hyecompany/vem-ui/styles.css";
```



```tsx
export function FileName() {
	return (
		<OverflowText
			text="quarterly-research-report-final.pdf"
			style={{ maxWidth: "12rem" }}
		/>
	);
}
```


While moving, text fades gently at the edges of its available space. The stationary label and the containing control stay crisp.

The component inherits typography and color. In a flex row, give the text space to shrink; avoid a parent whose minimum width is its entire content.

## Activate it from the whole control

Add `data-vem-overflow-trigger` to a containing button or option. Hovering or focusing that control activates the label. A parent with `data-highlighted` also activates it, so keyboard highlighting in a combobox works.


```tsx
export function ProjectButton() {
	return (
		<button
			type="button"
			data-vem-overflow-trigger=""
			style={{ maxWidth: "12rem" }}
		>
			<OverflowText text="development-services-europe" />
		</button>
	);
}
```


Use this behavior with your existing interaction component. OverflowText does not create a button, option, tooltip, or additional focus stop.

## Keep the name accessible

The complete string stays in the accessible text. Motion respects the user's reduced-motion preference. Text is shortened at grapheme boundaries, preserving emoji and combined characters.

Do not make animation the only way to read important content. For touch and reduced-motion users, show the full selected name in nearby details, allow a popup label to wrap, or provide an accessible disclosure. A native `title` alone is not a dependable touch alternative.

Measurements update after resizing and font loading. The first server render contains the full string; the stylesheet constrains it until the browser can measure.

[API reference](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.Function.OverflowText) · [All props](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.TypeAlias.OverflowTextProps) · [Spinner](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/spinner)


---

# Sheet

Open a focused task beside the current page.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/sheet


Import from `@hyecompany/vem-ui` after [adding the package](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui#add-the-package).

### Preview: Sheet

Open a focused task beside the current page. The example uses the public package component. Reset restores its initial state.

## Use it


```tsx
import {
	Button,
	Sheet,
	SheetClose,
	SheetContent,
	SheetDescription,
	SheetHeader,
	SheetTitle,
	SheetTrigger,
} from "@hyecompany/vem-ui";
export function SheetExample() {
	return (
		<Sheet>
			<SheetTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>
				Board details
			</SheetTrigger>
			<SheetContent>
				<SheetHeader>
					<SheetTitle>Weekend board</SheetTitle>
					<SheetDescription>
						A shared place for your next small adventure.
					</SheetDescription>
				</SheetHeader>
				<div style={{ padding: "1rem" }}>
					<p>Three tasks are ready to plan.</p>
					<SheetClose render={<Button />}>Done</SheetClose>
				</div>
			</SheetContent>
		</Sheet>
	);
}
```


## Behavior and choices

SheetTrigger opens SheetContent; SheetClose dismisses it. Keep a SheetTitle and, when useful, SheetDescription inside the content. The dialog handles focus, Escape, and returning focus to the trigger.

Use `side` on SheetContent to select the edge. Use controlled `open` and `onOpenChange` when another part of the application owns visibility. Keep forms and their state in your application; dismissing a sheet does not save a draft.

[API reference](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.Function.Sheet)

# Skeleton

Reserve space while initial content is unavailable.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/skeleton


Import from `@hyecompany/vem-ui` after [adding the package](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui#add-the-package).

### Preview: Skeleton

Reserve space while initial content is unavailable. The example uses the public package component. Reset restores its initial state.

## Use it


```tsx
import { Skeleton } from "@hyecompany/vem-ui";
export function SkeletonExample() {
	return (
		<section
			aria-busy="true"
			aria-label="Loading task summary"
			style={{ display: "grid", gap: "0.5rem", maxWidth: "18rem" }}
		>
			<Skeleton
				aria-hidden="true"
				style={{ height: "1.25rem", width: "70%" }}
			/>
			<Skeleton aria-hidden="true" style={{ height: "0.75rem" }} />
			<Skeleton
				aria-hidden="true"
				style={{ height: "0.75rem", width: "85%" }}
			/>
		</section>
	);
}
```


## Behavior and choices

Set the shape with ordinary CSS. Keep decorative placeholders hidden from assistive technology and describe the ongoing work once on their container.

Use a skeleton for initial acquisition, not to replace useful cached content. [QueryStatus](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/query-status) can explain revalidation beside values already on screen.

# Spinner

Show progress without taking focus away from an action.

URL: https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/spinner


Use a spinner beside a readable activity label. It inherits the current text color and has small, medium, and large sizes.

### Preview: Loading feedback

Choose a size and activate Load tasks to show progress inside the button. The button keeps a readable loading label; its spinner is decorative. The example returns to idle after a short delay.

[Add the package](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui#add-the-package) first. Import its components and include the stylesheet once:


```tsx
import { OverflowText, Spinner } from "@hyecompany/vem-ui";
import "@hyecompany/vem-ui/styles.css";
```



```tsx
export function SavingIndicator() {
	return <Spinner size="sm" aria-label="Saving changes" />;
}
```


The defaults are medium size and the accessible label “Loading”.

## Give progress a name

When adjacent text already says what is happening, make the spinner decorative with `aria-hidden="true"`. For a standalone spinner, supply `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` describing the activity.

A spinner communicates ongoing work; it does not manage requests, timing, or completion announcements. Keep the label tied to the actual activity, and use a status region when the result needs to be announced.

Reduced-motion preferences disable the animation while leaving its visual indicator and accessible label available.

[API reference](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.Function.Spinner) · [All props](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/reference/api/index.TypeAlias.SpinnerProps) · [OverflowText](https://hyevem.com/docs/ui/components/overflow-text)
